senses.sense_definition: An attitude, tone, or remark characterized by mocking irreverence, sarcasm, or snide criticism.

examples.text: Her online reviews were full of biting <w>snark</w> rather than constructive feedback.
He replied with unprovoked <w>snark</w>, which instantly offended everyone in the room.

traits.comment: Informal usage often seen in popular media and online commentary

senses.sense_definition: An elusive or impossible target of a search, referring allusively to a fruitless quest.

examples.text: Searching for that missing manuscript turned out to be an exhausting hunt for a <w>snark</w>.
The detectives soon realized that chasing the anonymous caller was like hunting a <w>snark</w>.

traits.comment: Literary allusion primarily found in specialized or older literary contexts

senses.sense_definition: An unrepeatable detection or fluked result in a scientific experiment.

examples.text: The physicists feared that the anomalous signal was merely a <w>snark</w>.
Subsequent laboratory trials failed to replicate the observation, proving it was just a <w>snark</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A connected graph where every vertex has three edges, which cannot be edge-colored with three colors.

examples.text: The Petersen graph is the smallest non-trivial example of a <w>snark</w>.
The mathematician published a paper examining edge colorings of every known <w>snark</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge, a cryptographic zero-knowledge proof.

examples.text: The new privacy blockchain relies heavily on a zero-knowledge <w>SNARK</w> to verify transactions.
Implementing a reliable <w>SNARK</w> requires careful mathematical verification and cryptographic assumptions.

senses.sense_definition: To make sarcastic, mocking, or snide remarks.

examples.text: She tended to <w>snark</w> whenever her colleagues proposed ideas she disliked.
Critics continued to <w>snark</w> about the director's latest film on social media.

senses.sense_definition: To snort or make a snorting sound.

examples.text: The horse began to <w>snark</w> loudly as it approached the unfamiliar fence.
He would occasionally <w>snark</w> in his sleep whenever he was congested.

traits.comment: Regional or dialectal variation of snort

senses.sense_definition: A fictional, elusive creature featured in Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem.

examples.text: The crew set sail across the sea in search of the mythical <w>Snark</w>.
Lewis Carroll introduced the bizarre <w>Snark</w> to readers in his famous poem.

senses.sense_definition: A sailboat constructed by author Jack London for his voyage across the Pacific Ocean.

examples.text: Jack London chronicled his adventurous voyage aboard the <w>Snark</w> in a travel memoir.
Constructing the <w>Snark</w> took far more money and time than London had anticipated.
